root_cause.text: The commit ab4f21e6fb1c incorrectly changed the protocol family of several xtables matches (mac, owner, physdev, realm) from NFPROTO_IPV4/IPV6 to NFPROTO_UNSPEC, allowing them to be used in contexts (like ebtables) where they are not applicable, leading to potential misuse or security issues.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reverts the family fields of xt_mac, xt_owner, xt_physdev from NFPROTO_UNSPEC to per-protocol registrations for IPv4 and IPv6, and xt_realm from NFPROTO_UNSPEC to NFPROTO_IPV4, citing that these extensions are not used by ebtables and xt_realm is IPv4-specific.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor mac match registration to use per-family entries (IPv4 and IPv6) instead of a single NFPROTO_UNSPEC entry, updating init/exit to use array-based registration.
intent_record.what: Replaced a single struct xt_match with an array of two struct xt_match entries, one for NFPROTO_IPV4 and one for NFPROTO_IPV6, and updated registration/unregistration functions from xt_register_match/xt_unregister_match to xt_register_matches/xt_unregister_matches using ARRAY_SIZE.
intent_record.how: The mac match is now explicitly registered for IPv4 and IPv6 protocol families instead of the previous NFPROTO_UNSPEC. This ensures the match is only available for IP traffic and aligns with typical per-family registration practices, without changing the match logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split the owner match registration into per-family matches to correct its scope from NFPROTO_UNSPEC to explicit IPv4 and IPv6 families.
intent_record.what: Changed the single xt_match structure owner_mt_reg with family NFPROTO_UNSPEC to an array of two xt_match structures with families NFPROTO_IPV4 and NFPROTO_IPV6, and updated registration/deregistration to use xt_register_matches/xt_unregister_matches with the array and its size.
intent_record.how: The owner match is now registered as two separate matches for IPv4 and IPv6 instead of a single match for all protocols. This restricts the owner match to only apply to IPv4 and IPv6 traffic, potentially preventing unintended matches on other address families.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the physdev match per IPv4 and IPv6 family to fix incorrect UNSPEC family registration.
intent_record.what: Replaced a single static struct xt_match with an array of two structs, one for NFPROTO_IPV4 and one for NFPROTO_IPV6, and updated registration/unregistration to use xt_register_matches/xt_unregister_matches with ARRAY_SIZE.
intent_record.how: The physdev match is now registered explicitly for IPv4 and IPv6 separately, rather than as UNSPEC, which allows the kernel to treat it per protocol family. The match behavior remains the same, but registration is now family-specific.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict xt_realm match to IPv4 family to fix incorrect handling on non-IPv4 protocols.
intent_record.what: Changed the .family field in realm_mt_reg from NFPROTO_UNSPEC to NFPROTO_IPV4.
intent_record.how: This restricts the xt_realm match to IPv4 only, ensuring it is not applied to non-IPv4 packets and preventing potential misuse or incorrect behavior.

relevance_review.reason: The group corrects the protocol family for the mac match from NFPROTO_UNSPEC to per-family entries (IPv4/IPv6), directly addressing the root cause of the vulnerability.

Group 1 directly addresses the root cause by splitting per-family registrations for owner and physdev matches, correcting their scope from NFPROTO_UNSPEC back to explicit IPv4 and IPv6 families, which is the exact issue described in the vulnerability.
The group directly addresses the vulnerability by restricting the xt_realm match to IPv4, correcting the incorrect change to NFPROTO_UNSPEC.
